# 1 Clement Chapter 52 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 52

---

## Council Notes

**On "confess" / "acknowledge" / "praise" (vv.1–2):** EMET: "confess." LOGOS: "acknowledge." PNEUMA: "praise." The Greek *exomologeomai* has a range: confess, acknowledge publicly, give thanks/praise. In v.1, the context is God's pleasure in human acknowledgment. "Confess" (EMET) is the traditional rendering and carries both senses of acknowledgment and thanksgiving. Retained.

**On "sacrifice of praise" / "sacrifice of thanksgiving" (v.4):** EMET: "sacrifice of praise." LOGOS: "sacrifice of praise." PNEUMA: "sacrifice of thanksgiving." The Greek *thysian aineseōs* is literally "sacrifice of praise" — a recognized LXX term (cf. Ps 50:14 LXX). "Sacrifice of praise" retained.

**On "broken spirit" / "contrite spirit" (v.5):** EMET: "broken spirit." LOGOS: "contrite spirit." PNEUMA: "broken and humble spirit." The Greek *pneuma suntetrimmenon* means "crushed/broken spirit" (cf. Ps 51:17). "Broken spirit" (EMET) is the literal rendering of *suntetrimmenon*. PNEUMA adds "humble" — this is an interpretive addition not in the text. "Broken spirit" retained.

**On "grows horns and hooves" / "growing its horns and hooves" (v.2):** All agents render this image from LXX Ps 69/68. The image of a young calf developing its horns (ready for sacrifice) is vividly LXX. LOGOS "growing its horns" is the most natural English. Retained.

---

**52:1** Brothers, the Lord has no need of anything from any person; he requires nothing from any quarter; but he is pleased when he is confessed. For the holy David says:

**52:2** "I will confess the LORD, and it will please him more than a young calf that is growing its horns and hooves.

**52:3** Let the poor see and be glad."

**52:4** And again he says: "Sacrifice to God a sacrifice of praise, and render your vows to the Most High. And call upon me in the day of your affliction, and I will deliver you, and you shall glorify me."

**52:5** "For the sacrifice of God is a broken spirit."

---

*— SOPHIA*
